clue.text: Patron of the arts, catching cold, left beef

indicators.note: the patron of the arts is catching, so holding inside it, the abbreviations for cold and left

parts.note: a Muse is one of the nine goddesses who inspire the arts
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: An arts patron caught a chill and left a complaint behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beef' looks like a verb (to complain) but is the noun for brawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Beef is informal for brawn or physical strength, which is muscular power.

indicators.note: the couple word is consuming, so containing, the next two pieces

parts.note: to mate is to couple or pair up
in means popular or fashionable
E is short for ecstasy, the drug

explanation.surface: A pair at a show taking a fashionable drug.
explanation.definitionFit: A matinee is an afternoon performance, one kind of show.

clue.text: Old Bob to pound sea creature

parts.note: bob was slang for a shilling in old British money, abbreviated s
quid is British slang for a pound sterling

explanation.surface: Old Bob going to beat a creature of the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: Before 1971 a British shilling (a 'bob') was written s; 'Bob' looks like a name.
explanation.definitionFit: A squid is a ten-armed marine mollusc, a creature of the sea.

parts.note: lace is a delicate openwork fabric
rated means judged or assessed

explanation.surface: Torn cloth is given a valuation.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacerated means torn or gashed, as flesh might be ripped.

indicators.note: the letters of the words if Steve are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: Steve becomes cheerful only if something about him alters.
explanation.definitionFit: Festive describes a cheerful, celebratory mood, so it is a synonym for happy.

clue.text: Fit to take charge of political party's money management

indicators.note: taking charge of something here means holding it, so the fit word contains the party

parts.note: fine means healthy or fit
the ANC is the African National Congress, a South African political party

explanation.surface: A party considered fit to run the treasury.
explanation.definitionFit: Finance is the management of money, especially large sums.

parts.note: a rig is a set of equipment or apparatus

explanation.surface: A department showing off specialist kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Branch' suggests a division of an organisation; it is a twig.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprig is a small stem or twig, a little branch of a plant.

clue.text: It's essential to apprehend road user in the flesh

indicators.note: apprehending is seizing and holding, so the essential word holds the road user

parts.note: innate qualities are essential, inborn ones
a car is a user of the road

explanation.surface: Police must catch a motorist in person.
explanation.definitionFit: Incarnate means embodied, given bodily form, so present in the flesh.

parts.note: ED is short for editor, a senior journalist
to perish is to die

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor drowns in swirling water.
explanation.definitionFit: Eddies are swirling currents of water, small whirlpools.

clue.text: One joining fabric of a bowler

definitions.meaning: someone who sews seams together in cloth
in cricket a bowler who makes the ball deviate off its seam

explanation.surface: A seamstress turns out to be a cricketer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bowler' looks like a hat; in cricket a seam bowler moves the ball off its raised stitching.
explanation.definitionFit: A seamer is one who seams cloth and also a cricket bowler using seam movement.

clue.text: On the run, wilfully holding club or cudgel

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are holding the club abbreviation within them
doing something wilfully means doing it wildly, signalling the letters of on the run are mixed up

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs, the card suit

explanation.surface: A fugitive deliberately carries a weapon while escaping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wilfully' rearranges ONTHERUN, and 'holding' puts C (clubs) inside it to give TRUN-C-HEON.
explanation.definitionFit: A truncheon is a short heavy stick, the same thing as a cudgel used as a weapon.

indicators.note: the word for best is placed in the abbreviation for street

parts.note: RD is the abbreviation for road, standing in for street
an ace is the best of its kind

explanation.surface: Runners contested the title of the fastest along the street.
explanation.definitionFit: To race is to compete in a contest of speed, so raced is a past-tense synonym.

clue.text: Return to relieve an all-time low

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: to relieve someone of something is to rid them of it

explanation.surface: Coming back to give someone a break proves the lowest point ever.
explanation.definitionFit: The nadir is the lowest point reached, the very bottom of fortunes.

clue.text: Ermine age terribly in a zoo

indicators.note: terribly means in a bad way, so the letters of ermine age are badly jumbled

explanation.surface: A stoat's coat ages badly when kept in a zoo.
explanation.walkthrough: Ermine is the white winter fur of the stoat.
explanation.definitionFit: A menagerie is a collection of wild animals kept for display, essentially a zoo.

clue.text: Competitive rider always covers slit in jacket

indicators.note: the poetic word for always covers, or surrounds, the word for the slit

parts.note: e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, meaning always
a vent is a slit in the back or side of a jacket

explanation.surface: A horsewoman in competition always wears a jacket with a slit.
explanation.definitionFit: An eventer takes part in equestrian eventing competitions, so is a competitive horse rider.

clue.text: One dispatches journalist supporting one-time president

indicators.note: in a down clue the journalist sits below, supporting the pieces above it

parts.note: ex means former or one-time
an editor is a senior journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter backs a former head of state.
explanation.definitionFit: An expeditor hastens matters along, someone who dispatches business efficiently.

indicators.note: upset means overturned, so the letters of jail and he are turned about

parts.note: he, with the 's standing for is to join it to the indicator

explanation.surface: A man lands in prison and is distressed about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Elijah is an Old Testament prophet who challenged the priests of Baal.

parts.note: to import goods is to ship them in
une is French for a, the feminine form

explanation.surface: A badger is brought over by boat in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badger' looks like the animal; it is the verb, to pester.
explanation.definitionFit: To importune is to pester someone persistently, just as to badger is.

clue.text: Swims back to emergency room for a rest

indicators.note: back means going backwards, so the word for swims is reversed

parts.note: dips are short swims

explanation.surface: A swimmer returns to hospital to recover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a rest' suggests repose, but in snooker a spider is a raised cue rest.
explanation.definitionFit: In snooker and billiards a spider is a rest with tall legs for bridging over balls.

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so the first letter of referee is taken

parts.note: to anger someone is to upset them

explanation.surface: The referee annoys a Scottish football side from the off.
explanation.definitionFit: Rangers is a Glasgow football club, a Scottish team.

definitions.meaning: to pepper is to shower something all over, as with bullets or shot

explanation.surface: Someone carelessly sprays the vegetable patch.
explanation.definitionFit: Peppering a target means scattering shots over it; peppers are also capsicum vegetables.

parts.note: coppers are small coins, pence, abbreviated P
to reach is to get hold of or contact

explanation.surface: Police officers try to find where someone lives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coppers' suggests police; here it means copper coins, pence. 'address' is the verb, to speak to.
explanation.definitionFit: To preach is to deliver a sermon, that is to address a congregation.

clue.text: Swimmer lacks time for theatre worker

indicators.note: lacks means is without, so the time letter is removed from the fish

parts.note: a sturgeon is a fish, which swims

explanation.surface: A swimmer is short of time for the stage worker's role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'theatre' means an operating theatre, not a playhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon works in the operating theatre of a hospital.

parts.note: pop is an informal name for father; the 's stands for is
off means gone away or departed

explanation.surface: Dad has left to die.
explanation.definitionFit: To pop off is an informal idiom for dying suddenly.

indicators.note: the dance word keeps, or holds inside it, the word for batting

parts.note: to bob is to bounce up and down, a sort of dance
in cricket the side batting is said to be in

explanation.surface: Two men named Bill and Bob, one of them at the crease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' and 'Bob' look like names; Bill is a draft law and bob a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordinance is a law or decree, and a bill is a proposed law.

definitions.note: the definition reads 'she is', a female who fits the answer

indicators.note: the agreeable word, when taking the drug, holds it inside

parts.note: nice means pleasant or agreeable
E is short for ecstasy, the drug

explanation.surface: A woman is pleasant only when on drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is a brother's or sister's daughter, always female, so a she.

definitions.meaning: the answer to 13 across is a horse ..., so this is one who rides
a clause added to a contract or bill that adds a stipulation

explanation.walkthrough: '13's' reads as '13 is': 13 across is EVENTER, a competitive horse rider.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider is someone on horseback and also an added clause or stipulation in a document.

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of delinquent

parts.note: rips are tears or slashes

explanation.surface: A gang leader attacks the weaklings with a knife.
explanation.definitionFit: Drips is informal for feeble, spineless people, the same as wimps.

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh version, so the letters of route are rearranged

explanation.surface: A newly opened road is wonderful.
explanation.definitionFit: Outré means bizarre or unconventional, matching the sense of fantastic as fanciful.

indicators.note: the unknown and the Tory are set in the word for baffling

parts.note: something elusive baffles the mind, hard to grasp
X is the standard unknown in algebra
C is the abbreviation for Conservative, the party of the Tories

explanation.surface: A mystery Conservative figures in a perplexing scandal story.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclusive is a story only one paper has, typically a revealing exposé.

clue.text: Penny is in the Army & Navy getting surgical equipment

indicators.note: the penny letter is in the word for the services

parts.note: the army and navy are the armed forces

explanation.surface: Penny joins the services and is issued with medical kit.
explanation.definitionFit: Forceps are pincers used by surgeons and obstetricians for gripping.

parts.note: having fewer clothes means having less on, giving less
if you are wearing something, you have it on

explanation.surface: Working out with hardly anything on.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'wearing fewer clothes' as 'having LESS ON'.
explanation.definitionFit: A lesson can be an exercise set for a pupil, a unit of teaching.
